lead.t: Obesity: excess body fat that impairs health, usually expressed as a body‑mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m² in adults; for Kenyan adults BMI ≥ 30 is the cut‑off, with waist‑circumference > 102 cm (men) or > 88 cm (women) indicating central adiposity.

qs.q: A 58-year-old man with well-controlled hypertension and a body mass index of 32 kg/m² is scheduled for elective inguinal hernia repair. What is his American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status class?
qs.e: ASA II describes a patient with mild systemic disease, which includes well-controlled hypertension, smoking, or obesity. ASA III is reserved for severe systemic disease that limits activity.

qs.q: According to the provided BMI classifications, how is a patient with a measured Body Mass Index of 38 kg/m² categorized?
qs.e: An obese BMI is classified in the range of 30 to 39.9, whereas morbid obesity requires a BMI of 40 or greater. Therefore, a BMI of 38 falls strictly into the obese category.
